This aligns with the textbook description that alveolar consolidation typically shows hyperechoic punctate areas (air bronchograms), whereas collapsed lung segments may resemble consolidation *without* air bronchograms [1, 2]. Thus, the key difference is the **presence and prominence of air bronchograms in A versus their relative absence or subtlety in B**.

Alveolar consolidation appears as an area of poorly defined dark, i.e. hypoechoic, lung tissue resembling liver called hepatization. Patient position
